Description: Institutional Review Board review and approval for human subjects research
When_Needed: Any research involving human participants (interviews; surveys; observations; biosamples)
Key_Actions: 1. Complete CITI training; 2. Develop protocol; 3. Write consent form; 4. Submit to IRB; 5. Respond to queries; 6. Receive approval
Documentation: IRB approval letter; protocol summary; consent form
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Research suspension; disqualification; legal liability; publication rejection
Resources: CITI Training; IRB office; institutional policy; OHRP

Description: Ensure participants understand study and voluntarily agree
Key_Actions: 1. Provide clear explanation of purpose; 2. Describe procedures; 3. Explain risks/benefits; 4. Ensure voluntary; 5. Obtain signature or affirmation
Documentation: Signed/documented consent; IRB approval; consent form copies
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Research suspension; publication rejection; legal liability
Resources: IRB guidelines; ICMJE standards; institutional templates

Description: Protect participant privacy and sensitive information
When_Needed: All human subjects research with identifiable data
Key_Actions: 1. De-identify data; 2. Use codes/ID numbers; 3. Maintain key separately; 4. Limit access; 5. Secure storage; 6. Document procedures
Documentation: De-identification log; access log; code key (secured separately)
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Legal liability; publication rejection; loss of trust; potential criminal charges

Description: Additional protections for vulnerable groups (children; prisoners; pregnant women; fetuses; cognitively impaired)
When_Needed: Research involving legally vulnerable or cognitively vulnerable populations
Key_Actions: 1. Develop additional safeguards; 2. Justify inclusion; 3. Minimize risk; 4. Seek assent; 5. Involve advocates if needed; 6. Enhance monitoring
Documentation: IRB protocol with enhanced safeguards; documentation of vulnerability assessment
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Research suspension; additional penalties for vulnerable population harm

Description: Safeguard sensitive and personal information from unauthorized access
When_Needed: Research with sensitive data (health; financial; demographic; biometric)
Key_Actions: 1. Implement encryption; 2. Use access control; 3. Apply de-identification; 4. Secure transmission; 5. Limit access; 6. Create audit trails
Documentation: Encryption certificates; access logs; data handling plan; security audit results
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Data breach liability; fines under GDPR/HIPAA; publication rejection; legal liability

Description: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act compliance for protected health information (PHI)
When_Needed: Research with U.S. health data or health information
Key_Actions: 1. Complete HIPAA training; 2. Develop Business Associate Agreement if needed; 3. Use de-identification; 4. Implement safeguards; 5. Document compliance
Documentation: HIPAA training certificate; BAA; de-identification documentation; compliance audit
Resources: 000 per violation); legal liability; publication rejection

Description: General Data Protection Regulation compliance for EU resident data
When_Needed: Research with data of EU residents
Key_Actions: 1. Conduct DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment); 2. Document legal basis; 3. Ensure consent; 4. Implement data subject rights; 5. Establish DPA; 6. Notify DPO
Documentation: DPIA documentation; consent records; DPA; Data protection policy
Responsible_Party: Data controller (researcher); Institutional legal; Data Protection Officer
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Fines up to €20 million or 4% global revenue; legal liability; publication rejection

Description: Identify and manage financial/personal interests that could bias research
When_Needed: All research with potential financial interests (funding source; employment; equity)
Key_Actions: 1. Complete COI disclosure form; 2. Identify interests; 3. Develop management plan; 4. Recuse if necessary; 5. Document management; 6. Update annually
Documentation: COI disclosure form; management plan; recusal documentation
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Publication rejection; retraction; loss of funding; reputation damage; legal action

Description: Ensure ethical publication practices and responsible dissemination
Key_Actions: 1. Disclose funding; 2. Declare author contributions; 3. Declare COI; 4. Provide data availability; 5. Avoid plagiarism; 6. Proper attribution; 7. Respect embargoes
Documentation: Publication manuscript; declarations; data availability statement; funding acknowledgment
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Publication rejection; retraction; authorship disputes; career damage; legal liability

Description: Ensure fair recognition and documentation of contributor contributions
Key_Actions: 1. Discuss authorship criteria upfront; 2. Document contributions; 3. Use CRediT taxonomy; 4. Obtain agreement; 5. Update as needed
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Authorship disputes; publication retraction; reputation damage; legal action

Description: Avoid reproducing others' work without attribution
Key_Actions: 1. Cite sources correctly; 2. Use quotation marks; 3. Paraphrase with citation; 4. Use plagiarism checker; 5. Train on proper attribution; 6. Maintain source records
Documentation: Plagiarism check report; source documentation; properly cited manuscript
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Publication rejection; retraction; dismissal; loss of degree; reputation damage; legal liability

Description: Conduct research honestly without fabrication; falsification; or deception
Key_Actions: 1. Follow research protocols; 2. Document decisions; 3. Avoid p-hacking; 4. Pre-register analysis; 5. Report null findings; 6. Respond to inconsistencies; 7. Seek guidance when uncertain
Documentation: Lab notebook; protocol documentation; preregistration; analysis plan; communication records
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Retraction; loss of funding; career termination; legal action; institutional sanctions

Description: Ethical use of animals in research (if applicable)
Key_Actions: 1. Complete IACUC training; 2. Submit protocol to IACUC; 3. Justify animal use; 4. Minimize harm/distress; 5. Use alternatives when possible; 6. Ensure humane euthanasia if needed
Documentation: IACUC approval letter; protocol; training certificate; vet oversight documentation
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Research suspension; legal liability; publication rejection; facility inspection findings

Description: Disclose funding sources and conflicts of interest
When_Needed: All research with external funding or conflicts
Key_Actions: 1. Identify funding source; 2. Disclose in publications; 3. Declare in presentations; 4. Include in manuscripts; 5. Update as funding changes
Documentation: Funding acknowledgment; publication declarations; grant documentation; funding source records
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Publication rejection; retraction; reputation damage; funder sanctions

Description: Complete Responsible Conduct of Research training
When_Needed: Required for most research; particularly grant-funded
Key_Actions: 1. Complete institutional RCR training; 2. Document completion; 3. Renew as required (typically every 3-5 years); 4. Choose discipline-specific if available
Documentation: RCR training certificate; training completion record
Timeline: Before conducting research; renew per institutional requirements
Penalties_for_Non-Compliance: Ineligibility for funding; publication rejection; institutional sanctions
